title: Members vote to fund 30 new gardens in food deserts
author: Grace Holloway, Executive Director
excerpt: At the September members' meeting, 1,214 members voted to put half of all Supporter dues toward new gardens where fresh food is hardest to find.
body:
The vote passed with 91 percent in favour. Starting in January, half of every Supporter membership goes into a dedicated fund for new gardens in neighbourhoods without a grocery store within a mile.

Chapters can apply for up to $8,000 per garden. The first round opens on 15 January.

title: Twin Cities Growers break their seed swap record
author: Erik Lindqvist
excerpt: More than 9,000 seed packets changed hands at the spring swap, and the fall swap is next month.
body: Volunteers counted 9,412 packets, up from 6,100 last year. Natives were the most popular table for the first time.

title: What the new city garden ordinances mean for you
author: Commonground Policy Team
excerpt: Six cities changed their rules on rain barrels, compost and selling produce this year. Here is what changed and what to do.
body: We read the ordinances so you don't have to. The short version: most changes help gardens, but two cities now require a permit for compost bins over a certain size.

title: Garden Group cover now includes volunteer days
author: Member Services
excerpt: Liability cover for Garden Group members now applies to volunteer workdays as well as public events.
body: Starting this month, the $1M general liability cover included with Garden Group membership also applies to scheduled volunteer days. No action needed if your group is already a member.

title: Five fall crops that forgive beginners
author: Mei Tanaka, Bay Commons
excerpt: Garlic, kale, radishes, spinach and fava beans: hard to kill and good to eat.
body: If you have never grown in the fall, start with these five. Each one shrugs off a missed watering and a cold snap.

title: Welcome, Austin Shared Harvest
author: Grace Holloway, Executive Director
excerpt: Our eighth chapter grew 11 tonnes of produce for local pantries in its first full year.
body: Austin Shared Harvest becomes a full chapter this month after a year as a provisional group.
